candidates.prompt: A common raven (Corvus corax), one adult bird standing on the ground with its wings folded against the body. Realistic anatomy and proportions: a large all-black corvid about 60 cm long, thick neck with shaggy throat hackles, a heavy, deep, slightly arched black bill about as long as the head, nasal bristles covering the base of the upper bill, dark eyes. Glossy black plumage with layered feathers; folded wing tips reach near the end of the tail; long wedge-shaped tail. Strong black legs with scaled tarsi and four clawed toes, three forward and one back, flat on the ground. Neutral standing pose, no base, no perch, no rock. Game-ready asset, clean closed mesh.

candidates.review: Side silhouette reads as a raven: heavy arched bill with a culmen ridge, shaggy throat hackles, crown and eye, layered wing coverts and primaries, long tapered tail, scaled legs with clawed toes (three forward, a hind toe). Faults: the wings stand off the flanks at the shoulders (body 0.32 m wide at raven scale against about 0.2 m), so it looks puffed or mantling rather than sleek; posture is a forward hunch; the tail is long and tapered in plan but the wedge is weak; nasal bristles are only hinted by feather shards; the underside between the legs is messy. Topology is remesher triangle soup with many feather shards and 3% slivers; 14 pieces once UV seams are welded. Fine for decimation to about 2,000 / 1,000 / 300 triangles.

accuracy_notes: Ravens here are told from crows by size, the heavy bill, the shaggy throat, the wedge-shaped tail in flight and soaring. The current player model (wings spread) has no feet detail and a generic bill; the Meshy candidate has the right bill and throat but the wings are too loose. A local birder should check bill depth, throat hackles, tail shape and the standing posture (ravens walk, and hop when hurried).
